# Lock file specification

`llm-proxy plugin install` writes `llm-proxy.lock.hcl` adjacent to your
configuration file (or inside the config directory when a directory is used).
It records the **concrete resolved version** and SHA-256 checksum for every
declared plugin on the current platform. Commit this file to version control
for reproducible deployments.

`llm-proxy serve` verifies the cached binary checksum against the lock file at
startup.

## Format

```hcl
# llm-proxy.lock.hcl — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND
# Generated by `llm-proxy plugin install`.

plugin "<label>" {
  source   = "github.com/<org>/llm-proxy-provider-<name>"
  version  = "~> 1.0"       # constraint from config
  resolved = "1.2.3"        # concrete version selected
  platform = "darwin_arm64" # os_arch at resolution time
}
```

| Field      | Description                                                |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`   | Mirrors the `source` field from the `plugin` block.        |
| `version`  | Mirrors the version constraint from the `plugin` block.    |
| `resolved` | The concrete version that was selected and downloaded.     |
| `platform` | The `GOOS_GOARCH` value at the time `plugin install` ran.  |

## Resolution priority

Each `plugin install` run resolves in this order (first hit wins):

1. **Lock file** — if an entry for the plugin and current `os_arch` platform
   exists, that version is used without any network call or cache scan.
2. **Local cache** — the highest installed version satisfying the version
   constraint is used; no download occurs.
3. **Remote registry** — for `github.com` sources the GitHub Releases API is
   queried and the highest matching release is selected; the archive is then
   downloaded and extracted.

Download is skipped when the resolved version is already present in the cache
for the current platform, regardless of how the version was resolved.

## Per-platform entries

Each `plugin install` run records the resolution for the current `GOOS_GOARCH`
only. A lock file may contain multiple entries for the same plugin label with
different `platform` values — one per developer machine or CI environment that
has run `plugin install`. Entries for other platforms are preserved as-is and
never overwritten by the current run.

## Upgrading

Pass `--upgrade` to bypass both the lock file and the local cache during
version resolution. The remote registry is always consulted and the latest
version satisfying the configured constraint is selected, even if an older
compatible version is already cached or locked.

```sh
llm-proxy plugin install --upgrade
```

Behaviour under `--upgrade`:

- The lock file entry for the current platform is **ignored** for resolution;
  the remote registry is always queried.
- The local binary download is still **skipped** when the remote-resolved
  version is already present in the cache (idempotent re-runs).
- The lock file is **updated** with the newly resolved version after the run.
- Entries for other platforms in the lock file are **preserved** untouched.

> `--upgrade` has no effect on exact-version pins (`version = "1.2.3"`) —
> the pin is always authoritative.

## Version constraint syntax

The `version` field in a `plugin` block follows Terraform's constraint syntax.
A constraint is one or more comma-separated conditions, **all of which must
hold** (logical AND):

| Operator                 | Meaning                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `= 1.2.3` or `1.2.3`    | Exact match — no API call needed                                  |
| `!= 1.2.3`               | Any version except this one                                       |
| `> 1.2.3` / `>= 1.2.3`  | Strictly greater / greater or equal                               |
| `< 2.0.0` / `<= 2.0.0`  | Strictly less / less or equal                                     |
| `~> MAJOR.MINOR`         | `>= MAJOR.MINOR.0, < (MAJOR+1).0.0`                              |
| `~> MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`   | `>= MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, < MAJOR.(MINOR+1).0`                      |

Multiple conditions: `">= 1.2.0, < 2.0.0"` (comma-separated, logical AND).

**GitHub sources:** range constraints query the GitHub Releases API and select
the highest matching `v*` tag (draft and pre-release tags are excluded).

**Non-GitHub sources** only support exact version pins. A range constraint on a
`file://` or custom-URL source is an error at install time.

Pre-release versions (e.g. `1.0.0-rc.1`) are never selected by range
constraints; use an exact pin to target one: `= 1.0.0-rc.1`.
